items.name: panel
items.title: Panel
items.description: The one floating surface: nk-panel with a header (title, description, actions, optional tabs row), a scrolling body and a footer.

spec.role: The one floating surface: a menu, a form, a list on the game.
rules: One primary action per panel.
Rows inside, not cards.
Positioned by anchors and zones, never absolute pixels.

items.name: edge-sheet
items.title: Edge Sheet
items.description: A full-height sheet flush to a screen edge, the pause menu backdrop and the ox_lib context sheet as one component: stock Sheet (non-modal) in the panel surface, hairline on the open edge, inner column, section-size title with optional back and close buttons, sub-pages that swap in place, a level traced along the header edge, staggered slide-in and a faster exit.

spec.role: A sheet from a screen edge: an inventory side, a context menu.
spec.level: the edge line: a fill such as weight (EdgeSheetEdge value, 0–100).
rules: The game stays visible beside it.
Positioned on an edge, never centred with a transform.

items.name: nui-image
items.title: NUI Image
items.description: The picture of an item, clothing, vehicle or weapon by the conventions popular servers use (ox/qb/ps/lj inventories, FiveM docs vehicles, clothing packs by template): candidate URLs from nuikit-core resolveImage, lazy, an onError chain, an icon when none load.

items.name: menu-row
items.title: Menu Row
items.description: The 40px action row: icon, label, description, a progress bar in any tone or colour, and a trailing meta, chevron, Kbd, checkbox or value stepper. Active, disabled and destructive. MenuRowList slides one indicator to the active row. MenuRowDetails shows metadata with per-item bar colours.

spec.role: The action row every list is made of.
anatomy: one trailing thing: meta | chevron | kbd | checkbox | stepper | actions
spec.level: progress: the row's progress line (0–1 of its value).
rules: States on data-state: rest, focus (active), confirm (on click), disabled, alert.
Hover is the accent; focus is the identity's indicator, never the hover colour.
A list the UI drives slides one indicator (MenuRowList).

items.name: stat
items.title: Stat
items.description: A label over a tabular number that matters (cash, players, a timer), in three sizes, with meta and a delta. On a panel or on the game.

items.name: meter
items.title: Meter
items.description: A slim bar on a theme or game track, with a caption and value, low/high thresholds that turn it destructive, and optional segments; timed runs; and the timed-progress slab (variant="slab": label, thin line, cancel key), the successor of task-progress.

spec.role: A level on a bar: health, fuel, weight, a timed action.
anatomy: meter (label row: icon, label, value text)
slab: label, cancel key, thin line
spec.level: value / max; a timed run fills 0 → 1 over duration (--level is its end state).
rules: Data is value/max or --level, never a variant.
Thresholds turn it destructive; tone never encodes data.
A timed run completes from a timer, so it finishes with motion off.

items.name: hud-chip
items.title: HUD Chip
items.description: An always-on pill or tile on the game world: icon and text; active (talking, selected) or warning.

spec.role: A small fact on the HUD: voice range, radio, seatbelt.
rules: Its shape prop is the form (pill, tile); corners follow data-nk-shape on an ancestor.
warning is the theme's destructive; active is primary.
data-hue carries its role; the theme colours it.

items.name: text-roll
items.title: Text Roll
items.description: A short text that changes like a slot reel: the old value rolls out and the new one in, masked to the line, with direction and per-character stagger; NumberRoll rolls each digit on its own (money, speed, ammo, clocks). Swaps at once when motion is off.

items.name: smooth-input
items.title: Smooth Input
items.description: Drop-ins for shadcn Input and Textarea: a caret that glides and breathes in the theme primary, and typed characters that ease in. The real field underneath (selection, IME, paste, forms); the native caret when motion is off.

items.name: vital
items.title: Vital
items.description: A player stat: an icon and a shadcn Progress, colored by a theme token. Pulses when low.

items.name: use-collapse
items.title: useCollapse
items.description: The collapse engine for clustered indicators: a change opens a chip for --nk-rest-delay, changes within 400 ms batch together, critical first then the biggest change, at most N then +N, per-key opt-outs. Pure state functions for tests.

items.name: collapse-stack
items.title: Collapse stack
items.description: A row of clustered indicators on the collapse engine: icons at rest, a change opens a chip, open chips lead (critical first, then the biggest change), at most max, then +N.

spec.role: Clustered indicators (vitals, voice, job status) that stay icons until something changes.
rules: At rest only icons; a change opens a chip for --nk-rest-delay.
Changes within the batch window (400 ms) open and close together.
Critical first, then the biggest change; at most max, then +N.
Order moves with CSS order; the DOM never re-orders, nothing remounts.

items.name: vital-chip
items.title: Vital Chip
items.description: The HUD status chip as composable parts (Root, Shape, Level, Icon, Label, Pop): one SVG path per shape (auto, square, rounded, circle, diamond, hex, chamfer) drives the surface, border, level trace, liquid fill and label anchors; level outline/fill/bar/none; label inline/tag/flag; a pop with the signed change. Themed by --nk-chip-shape, --nk-level-style, --nk-label-attach, --nk-vital-icon.

spec.role: One vital on the HUD: health, armor, hunger, thirst, stress.
anatomy: vital-chip-row (optional: chips that know each other)
rules: data-hue carries the vital's role (health, armor…).
The level style comes from the theme (outline, liquid, bar); the data never picks it.
Readable over a bright sky (legibility fixture).
display: pill (icon, name, value) | value | icon (level as fill) | expand (opens on a change, settles after --nk-rest-delay); the theme default is --nk-vital-display.
neighbours (a chip that opens, in a Row): push | collapse | overlay; the theme default is --nk-vital-neighbours.
expand chips in a VitalChip.Row open through the row's collapse engine (useCollapse): batched, ordered, capped at max with +N.

items.name: nui-menu
items.title: NUI Menu
items.description: Keyboard-first list menu: a shadcn Card of Items, highlighted with accent like shadcn menus.

items.name: radial-menu
items.title: Radial Menu
items.description: Action wheel in SVG (shadcn has no radial), styled like shadcn menus: popover, border, accent.

rules: Items draw data-state: focus (the pointed wedge), disabled.
Sub-menus open in place; Escape goes back a level.

items.name: speedometer
items.title: Speedometer
items.description: Vehicle gauge: SVG arc in primary/destructive, gear as a Badge, fuel as a Progress.

items.name: use-nui-store
items.title: useNuiStore
items.description: Merge partial updates from Lua into one object.

items.name: notice
items.title: Notice
items.description: A notification on the game (status icon, title, description, a time-left line that pauses on hover) and the stack that pins them to any of eight positions, with a useNotices() queue; an item add/remove slab (icon tile, name, delta) whose changes merge within 1.5 s. The default look of the notify intent.

spec.role: A notification on the game, and the stack that holds them.
anatomy: notice: status icon, title, description, time line, close
rules: Newest nearest the edge; at most five per position.
Slides in from its stack's edge, out toward it.
error is data-state alert.
Queue policy (useNotices / NuiNotices): stack or one at a time, a capped queue (the oldest waiting goes), shown ones hurry (dwell x hurry) while others wait.

items.name: form-field
items.title: Form field
items.description: One row of a game form (label, hint, description, error, required, inline value, reset) and a preset per value: text, number with stepper, select and multi-select, checkbox or switch, slider, date (typed, or a picker that steps up to years and decades), date range, time (12 or 24h), colour. Date range and time values in ox_lib's shapes (epoch ms). validateField() for required, min/max, length and order. The default look of the input intent; nothing relies on :has() or native pickers.

items.name: death-screen
items.title: Death Screen
items.description: Last stand and death over the game: a countdown and bar, call EMS, hold to respawn with a live bar, red at the edges. Wired to the death surface and the death:hold live value, with fixtures for every state.
items.docs: Mount <DeathScreenSurface /> in App.tsx and open it from Lua: nk.surface("death", { layer = "system", input = "none", hides = { "hud" } }):open(data). Stream the respawn hold with nk.stream("death:hold"). A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-death -- -t death-screen

items.name: hud-minimal
items.title: Minimal HUD
items.description: The always-on HUD: vitals and needs with voice, cash, bank and job, and a speedometer with seatbelt and engine warnings while driving. The player comes from nuikit's bridge (any framework); speed and rpm are live values.
items.docs: Mount <HudMinimalSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("hud", { layer = "hud" }) once nk.player.get().loaded, send hud:vehicle on change and stream hud:vehicle:speed and hud:vehicle:rpm with nk.stream. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-hud -- -t hud-minimal

items.name: confirm
items.title: Confirm
items.description: Are you sure? Title, body, cancel and one primary or destructive action, a running state and acknowledge-only. Escape cancels through the nuikit surface (not a private key handler); Enter presses the focused action; Tab stays inside. The default look of the confirm intent.

spec.role: A decision before something that can't be undone.
rules: Focus starts on the action; Escape and Cancel go back.
Destructive actions say so in the label.

items.name: key-prompt
items.title: Key prompt
items.description: "[E] Open garage": the prompt slab (key chip + verb) by default, or a panel or HUD surface; keys (none, one or a combination), label that truncates or wraps, description, icon; hold-to-confirm with a filling line, driven by Lua (progress) or by pointer and key when the page has focus; active and disabled; a stack for any edge. The default look of the prompt intent; supersedes key-hint.

spec.role: "[E] Open garage": what a key does here.
spec.level: the hold progress, 0 → 1 (Lua's progress, or the pointer/key hold).
rules: States: rest, focus (active), hold, confirm (when the hold fills), disabled.
In game Lua reads the key and sends progress; the page draws it.
One prompt per action; a stack for several.
The interaction ladder (stage): dormant (the key chip alone, quiet) → aware → focus → hold → confirm, on data-ladder; without stage, today's prompt.

items.name: progress-ring
items.title: Progress ring
items.description: A circle that fills: a level, or a timed run whose onComplete fires from a timer (never an animation event, so it works with motion off). Label, percentage or any centre, tones, a game or theme track, three sizes, a cancel hint. The round half of the progress intent; meter is the bar.

spec.role: A level or a timed run, round.
spec.level: value / max; a timed run fills 0 → 1.
rules: onComplete fires from a timer, never an animation event.
The round half of the progress intent; meter is the bar.

items.name: countdown
items.title: Countdown
items.description: A timer that matters: tabular mm:ss (h:mm:ss past an hour) in the identity's display type, a caption, a line that drains on its own between updates, a warning threshold, a done state, sizes up to a full-screen clock, theme or game surface. From Lua's seconds, or running on its own with onComplete from a timer.

items.name: band
items.title: Band
items.description: A full-width band for a state the player is in (incapacitated, cuffed, spectating): the game darkened and tinted by a tone, tone hairlines above and below, a display title and a caption. The band slab of design v2, pinned to the bottom or top edge or in the flow.

spec.role: A full-width state across the screen: incapacitated, wanted.
rules: One band at a time.
Text on the game: world foreground, legible over any frame.

items.name: money
items.title: Money
items.description: Every amount formatted one way: tabular figures, the server's currency and locale (Intl), whole units by default, sign auto/always/never, a direction tone for gains and losses, compact ($1.3M), or a plain number with a prefix or suffix. Inline, with formatMoney() for text.

items.name: item-slot
items.title: Item slot
items.description: One square of an inventory, shop, hotbar or crafting grid: image, name, count, hotkey or stock, price, a durability line, and the drag-and-drop states (empty, active, drop target, dragging, locked). Wells on a panel or the HUD surface for a hotbar.

spec.role: One slot of an inventory, hotbar or shop.
spec.level: durability, 0–100 as 0–1 (the line under the item).
rules: data-state: focus (active or drop target), disabled (locked); the slot's own state is data-slot-state.
Drag and drop stays with the caller.

items.name: player-card
items.title: Player card
items.description: Who someone is at a glance: avatar or initials, name, job and grade with an on/off duty dot and the words, a grid of stats (mono for codes), and footer actions. On the panel recipe.

items.name: empty-state
items.title: Empty state
items.description: When there's nothing to show or something went wrong: an icon, a short title, one sentence on what to do next, optional actions. Stock shadcn Empty on the kit's scale; empty or error tone; panel or screen size.

items.name: skill-check
items.title: Skill check
items.description: Press the key while the needle is in the zone: zone start and size (wrapping past 360°), speed, the key, a success or fail outcome. Runs itself (needle drawn per frame without re-rendering, a full turn is a miss) and reads the key, or takes the angle from outside. The default look of the challenge intent.

items.name: pause-menu
items.title: Pause Menu
items.description: Esc opens it in place of GTA's: the server and its actions (resume, map, settings, key bindings, disconnect with a confirm) on a rail, the player and the server on cards, the game blurred behind. Wired to the pause surface and one pause:action callback.
items.docs: Mount <PauseMenuSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, catch Esc (control 200), open nk.surface("pause", { layer = "modal", input = "full", exclusive = true, hides = { "hud" }, blockedBy = { "dead" } }) with a PauseMenuData table, and answer nk.on("pause:action"). A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-pause -- -t pause-menu

items.name: loading-screen
items.title: Loading Screen
items.description: The real load progress (the game's own load events, phase by phase), tips, links, backgrounds and music, in the server's nuikit theme handed over on connect. For a resource's loadscreen page.
items.docs: Mount <LoadingScreenPage /> in App.tsx of a resource whose fxmanifest has loadscreen 'web/dist/index.html' and loadscreen_manual_shutdown 'yes'. Hand it data from the server with deferrals.handover({ nuikit = { serverName, tips, theme = GlobalState.nuikitTheme, … } }). A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-loading -- -t loading-screen

items.name: settings
items.title: Settings
items.description: Player settings in one panel: toggles, choices, sliders and key hints in tabbed sections. Every change goes to Lua (settings:change) and the row shows what Lua answers; sliders send once, when let go.
items.docs: Mount <SettingsSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("settings", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true }) with a SettingsData table and answer nk.on("settings:change") with the value to show (and nk.on("settings:reset")). nk.prefs gives you UI size, reduced motion and high contrast for free. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-settings -- -t settings

items.name: scoreboard
items.title: Scoreboard
items.description: Who's online with server IDs, names, jobs and ping, a search by name, ID or job, how full the server is, and which activities can start given who's on duty. Read only: the scoreboard surface with a ScoreboardData snapshot.
items.docs: Mount <ScoreboardSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("scoreboard", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true }) with a ScoreboardData table ({ players = { { id, name, job, ping, you } }, max, activities }) and :update it while it's open. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-scoreboard -- -t scoreboard

items.name: garage
items.title: Garage
items.description: Your vehicles at a garage, filtered by stored, out and impounded, with the selected one's fuel, engine and body. Take out, store the one you're driving, release from the impound; Lua answers each and its errors show on the panel.
items.docs: Mount <GarageSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("garage", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true }) with a GarageData table and answer nk.on("garage:takeOut"), nk.on("garage:store") and nk.on("garage:release") with { ok, error }. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-garage -- -t garage

items.name: bank
items.title: Bank
items.description: Accounts, the selected one's balance and recent transactions, and deposit, withdraw and transfer in a dialog that checks the amount before Lua does. Protocol-agnostic; ATMs have no transfers.
items.docs: Mount <BankSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("bank", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true }) with a BankData table, answer nk.on("bank:deposit"), nk.on("bank:withdraw") and nk.on("bank:transfer") with { ok, error }, and :update it with fresh balances. Check every amount on the server. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-bank -- -t bank

items.name: job-menu
items.title: Job menu
items.description: Your job in one panel: a duty toggle and the job's actions; for the boss, a Staff tab with the job account, promote, demote, fire (with a confirm) and hire whoever is nearby. Protocol-agnostic.
items.docs: Mount <JobMenuSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("job", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true }) with a JobMenuData table, answer nk.on("job:duty"), nk.on("job:action"), nk.on("job:hire"), nk.on("job:fire") and nk.on("job:grade") with { ok, error }, and :update it after a change. Check every boss action on the server against the caller's own job and grade. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-jobs -- -t job-menu

items.name: job-sheet
items.title: Job sheet
items.description: The one frame for a resource's menu: a floating sheet (docs/design.md, Surfaces) with a header row, sections of 48px rows, sub-pages that swap in place with a back row, and one actions row with a single primary. Lua fills the pages; the server checks every row against the caller's own job, grade and duty. Protocol-agnostic.
items.docs: Mount <JobSheetSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("jobsheet", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true, escape = "back" }) with a JobSheetData table (the job and its pages), answer nk.on("jobsheet:duty") and nk.on("jobsheet:row") with { ok, error }, and :update it after a change. Check every row on the server against the caller's own job, grade and duty. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-job -- -t job-sheet

items.name: interaction
items.title: Interaction
items.description: How the player uses the world: a target eye at the centre of the screen with the options of what they aim at (chosen with the cursor or the scroll wheel), and key prompts near places with press or hold. Protocol-agnostic; Lua does the raycast and reads the keys.
items.docs: Mount <InteractionSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("target", { layer = "world", input = "none" }) with a TargetData table while the target key is held and :update it as the aim changes; open nk.surface("prompts", { layer = "hud", input = "none" }) with a PromptsData table near places and send hold progress. To choose with the mouse, open a cursor surface of your own, set picking = true and answer nk.on("interaction:select") with { ok, error }. Check anything that matters on the server. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-interaction -- -t interaction

items.name: shop
items.title: Shop
items.description: A catalogue grid by category with price and stock, a cart with steppers, cash or bank, and checkout with a confirm. The page checks the cart before asking; the server decides. Protocol-agnostic.
items.docs: Mount <ShopSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("shop", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true, escape = "back" }) with a ShopData table, answer nk.on("shop:buy") with { ok, error } and :update it with fresh stock and money. On the server, use your own prices and stock, check every line, and move money and items all or nothing. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-shop -- -t shop

items.name: inventory
items.title: Inventory
items.description: The player's items and a second container side by side: pointer-driven drag and drop (Shift half, Ctrl one), stack and swap, a tooltip, weight meters, use, and a hotbar with a HUD strip. Protocol-agnostic; Lua decides every move.
items.docs: Mount <InventorySurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("inventory", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true, hides = { "hotbar" } }) with an InventoryData table, answer nk.on("inventory:move") and nk.on("inventory:use") with { ok, error }, and :update it after each; open nk.surface("hotbar", { layer = "hud", input = "none" }) for a moment when a hotbar key is used. Check every move on the server. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-inventory -- -t inventory

items.name: vehicle-shop
items.title: Vehicle shop
items.description: A showroom: vehicles by category on the left edge (the real car stands behind), stats, a paint colour from swatches or any hex, cash or bank, a test drive, and buy with a confirm. Protocol-agnostic.
items.docs: Mount <VehicleShopSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("vehicle-shop", { layer = "panel", exclusive = true, escape = "back" }) with a VehicleShopData table; answer nk.on("vehicle-shop:preview") by showing that model and colour (a local car), and nk.on("vehicle-shop:test-drive") and nk.on("vehicle-shop:buy") with { ok, error }. On the server, use your own prices, spawn the car yourself and refund if it can't be delivered. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-dealership -- -t vehicle-shop

items.name: character-select
items.title: Character select
items.description: Who to play: character slots, the chosen one as a PlayerCard with Play and Delete (behind a destructive confirm), spawn points after Play, and a create form with the same rules the server checks. Protocol-agnostic.
items.docs: Mount <CharacterSelectSurface /> in App.tsx. In Lua, open nk.surface("character-select", { layer = "modal", exclusive = true, escape = "back" }) with a CharacterSelectData table when the player joins; answer nk.on("character:play"), nk.on("character:create") and nk.on("character:delete") with { ok, error }. On the server, check that the character is the caller's, that the spawn point is yours (send its coordinates), and that a new character is valid. A whole resource with the Lua: npm create nuikit@latest my-characters -- -t character-select

items.name: utils
items.title: cn (kit-aware)
items.description: lib/utils.ts with a cn() that knows the nk-* kit: a kit utility removes the earlier stock classes that set its colour or type (nk-chip-active after text-hud-foreground), and one type style, surface or anchor wins per element. Generated from kit.css; replaces shadcn's lib/utils.ts.
